descriptionHtml:
Bug B23 · P1 · known

Patient cards are missing fields: age shows '76y' not '76F', Hospital cards have no hospital day, Nursing Home cards no visit number

Tickets: TFA-92579 AC3–4 ready for qa · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: dev + local

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S03, TC-01/S05, TC-01/S26

Approach · TC-01 Patient Chart Card · S06 Nursing Home visit number keeps rising with admission age and visits, including past the 'last two visits' window

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U5 The card shows the hospital day (Hospital) or the visit number (Nursing Home). (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3)
  • U6 The day/visit number advances each calendar day by server time and never stays frozen; a device with a wrong clock or time zone shows the same number. (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 4; UAT 3.8)
  • U8 With multiple patients loaded, everything above holds in both Hospital and Nursing Home. (UAT TC-01; UAT 3.3)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given seededCensus N1 (admitted today, 0 prior visits), N3 (−3 d, 1 prior), N4 (−7 d, 2 prior), N5 (−14 d, 4 prior on distinct days; 3.6 keeps only the last two)

When Read each resident's visit number on the card (Today's Visits and All Residents)

Then N1 shows the first value; N1 < N3 < N4 < N5; N5 is above N4 even though only two of its visits are retained

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Q3-independent: N1 = the first value ('Visit 1' format per Q3) and strictly N1 < N3 < N4 < N5. A number counted from retained visits caps at 3 under 3.6 and fails N5 > N4; a frozen number fails the ordering. The comparison needs numbers read per card, so it lives in the card-scoped spec (S26); oracle.mjs only matches substrings. …

Where it ran: local newspec-a (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S06 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Known product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92579 ready for qa

Nursing Home resident cards show no visit number at all, so a resident on a fifth visit looks the same as one admitted today.

Evidence: newspec-a lane (N1/N3/N4/N5 seeded) plus the datasets lane. This is the visit-number half of dev report §2 #5 (C2, 'no hospital day / visit number', U27). The format is still open (Q3), but it does not matter because no number is shown.

Folded in: local datasets TC-01/S06 (same failure, folded into this result)

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-a.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-a.

UAT item: TC-01 Patient Chart Card · Section: A1 · Home Screen & Dashboard · Scenario: TC-01/S06

Nursing Home visit number keeps rising with admission age and visits, including past the 'last two visits' window

Tickets: TFA-92579 Home Screen: Patient Chart Card (ready for qa)

New local lane newspec-a: status failed in newspec-a/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue)).

How it is tested (newspec-a/plan.json, automatable: yes): Seed N1/N3/N4/N5 (and the S26 residents) on a fresh account with admitDate / addedAt back-dated and prior visits as snfVisitDates + previousNotes on distinct past server days (rows written through snf:add, the app's own mutation); open Today's Visits and All Residents, read each card's visit number (card-scoped). Oracle: a number is shown, N1 is the first value, strictly N1 < N3 < N4 < N5 (Q3-independent). — Seeding through snf:add accepts the visit-history fields; reading cards is a scripted browser step.

Detail:

N1 (admitted today, 0 prior), N3 (1 prior), N4 (2 prior), N5 (4 prior on distinct days) seeded on a fresh account; on Today's Visits and All Residents no card shows any visit number (no 'Visit N', 'Day N' or similar), so N1 < N3 < N4 < N5 cannot hold under either Q3 reading.

Product issue: A physician looking at the Nursing Home list sees no visit number on any resident card (cards show unit, age, stored diagnosis, status and admission badge only), so a resident on their 5th visit looks the same as one admitted today. Breaks UAT TC-01 Expected Result: 'the hospital day or visit number. The day/visit number advances each calendar day and must not stay frozen' (TFA-92579 AC 3/4).

Evidence: 4 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A (our scripted spec, not written yet): it would seed prior visits and read the cards through the local admin helpers (backend.ts, fresh @roundai.test accounts); dev has no admin key and one shared account, so it runs on the local stack only (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
